events.title: Cicero Is Assassinated
events.description: The Roman orator, lawyer and statesman Cicero was killed on the orders of the Second Triumvirate. His death came during the political purges that followed the assassination of Julius Caesar.
events.significance: Cicero's death is often seen as a symbolic end of the Roman Republic's free political debate. His speeches and letters are still studied as models of Latin prose and political rhetoric.

events.title: Royal Opera House Opens at Covent Garden
events.description: The Royal Opera House opened its doors in Covent Garden, London. It began as a theatre and grew into one of the world's best-known homes for opera and ballet.
events.significance: The venue became a cornerstone of British performing arts and remains a leading international stage nearly three centuries later.

events.title: Albert Einstein Is Granted a U.S. Visa
events.description: The German-born physicist Albert Einstein received an American visa. He was then one of the most famous scientists in the world, and Europe's politics were growing darker.
events.significance: The visa opened the way for Einstein's move to the United States. He took up a post at Princeton and became a leading figure among the many scientists who left Europe.

events.title: Attack on Pearl Harbor
events.description: Japanese forces launched a surprise air attack on the U.S. naval base at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii. The attack killed 2,403 Americans.
events.significance: The United States declared war on Japan the next day and entered World War II. The date is now observed each year as National Pearl Harbor Remembrance Day.

events.title: Apollo 17 Launches to the Moon
events.description: Apollo 17 lifted off from Cape Canaveral, Florida. It was the final crewed mission of the Apollo program.
events.significance: No human has traveled to the Moon since this flight. It remains the last time people have ventured beyond low Earth orbit.
